sources.entry: fasthtml - The fastest way to create an HTML app.

summary.one_liner: FastHTML is a Python web framework for building interactive, hypermedia-driven web apps by mapping HTML and HTTP directly to Python code and using HTMX for interactivity.
summary.what_it_does: FastHTML lets you write web apps as plain Python, with route functions decorated by a router (rt) that return HTML built from Python components. The README says its functionality maps 1:1 to HTML and HTTP. A minimal app is created with fast_app() and serve(), run with python main.py. Interactivity comes from HTMX attributes such as hx_get, so routes can return HTML partials that replace page elements without a full reload. The README also points to an LLM-friendly context file (/llms-ctx.txt) for AI coding assistants, plus links to documentation, an idiomatic example app, and a third-party gallery of components. It also lists related HTML-generation and hypermedia projects in other languages.
use_cases: create server-rendered HTML partials with HTMX
prototype a small web app quickly in Python
generate HTML in Python code instead of templates
how_to_run: Create main.py with: from fasthtml.common import *; app,rt = fast_app(); @rt('/') def get(): return Div(P('Hello World!'), hx_get="/change"); serve()
Open the printed local link in a browser
notable: Maps HTML elements and HTTP routes 1:1 to Python code
HTMX-based partial updates without writing JavaScript, per the README's examples
Ships an LLM-friendly context file (/llms-ctx.txt) for AI coding assistants
Built on fastcore.xml.FT for HTML components
caveats: README says the framework is new and not all features and patterns are documented yet; users may need to read source code and notebooks
README says component libraries installable via pip are planned for the future, not yet available
Its own text says AI assistants may not know it because it is newer than most LLMs
